instruments.name: Uilleann Pipes
instruments.note: Chanter in D; drones and regulators assumed in D; bellows-blown.

instruments.name: Irish Flute (simple-system)
instruments.note: Wooden simple-system flute in D; breathy tone and cuts/taps.

instruments.name: Bodhrán
instruments.note: Frame drum played with a tipper; pitch shaped by the hand behind the skin.

instruments.name: Irish Bouzouki
instruments.note: Flat-backed Irish adaptation from the late 1960s onward; GDAD or GDAE tuning assumed.

instruments.name: Concertina
instruments.note: Anglo or English system; 19th-century onward, avoid as a medieval default.

instruments.name: Great Highland Bagpipe
instruments.note: Nine-note chanter, pitch near Bb (written A); two tenor and one bass drone; no dynamics.

instruments.name: Scottish Smallpipes
instruments.note: Bellows-blown, quieter than the Highland pipe; chanter commonly in A or D.

instruments.name: Clàrsach (Gaelic harp)
instruments.note: Lever or wire-strung harp; wire-strung historical model rings long.

instruments.name: Welsh Triple Harp
instruments.note: Three rows of strings, chromatic inner row; gut strings.

instruments.name: Crwth
instruments.note: Historical bowed lyre; surviving instruments and tuning accounts are partial, so this is a reconstruction.

instruments.name: Concert Zither
instruments.note: Fretted melody strings plus open accompaniment strings; Munich or Vienna tuning.

instruments.name: Steirische Harmonika (diatonic accordion)
instruments.note: Push-pull diatonic button accordion with Helikon bass.

instruments.name: Germanic Round Lyre (reconstruction)
instruments.note: Speculative reconstruction after archaeological finds (e.g. Trossingen, Sutton Hoo); string count and tuning unknown.

instruments.name: Bone Flute (reconstruction)
instruments.note: Reconstructed from archaeological finds; hole spacing gives non-tempered pitches.

instruments.name: Wooden Duct Flute (reconstruction)
instruments.note: Speculative wooden duct/end-blown flute; pitch set is an assumption.

instruments.name: Hardanger Fiddle (Hardingfele)
instruments.note: Four playing strings plus sympathetic understrings; many traditional scordaturas.

instruments.name: Nyckelharpa
instruments.note: Keyed fiddle with sympathetic strings; modern chromatic form assumed.

instruments.name: Kantele
instruments.note: Plucked zither; 5-string diatonic to concert models; tuning configurable.

instruments.name: Tagelharpa (reconstructed)
instruments.note: Horsehair-strung bowed lyre; modern revival draws on Estonian hiiu kannel and Finnish jouhikko.

instruments.name: Flamenco Guitar
instruments.note: Low action, golpeador tap plate; capo commonly used.

instruments.name: Palmas (hand claps)
instruments.note: Sordas (muted) and claras (bright) hand claps following compás.

instruments.name: Hurdy-Gurdy (vielle à roue)
instruments.note: Wheel-bowed with drone and trompette (buzzing bridge) strings; drone tuning configurable.

instruments.name: Tamburello
instruments.note: Large frame drum with jingles for tarantella and pizzica.

instruments.name: Kaval
instruments.note: End-blown rim flute with a strong overblown upper register.

instruments.name: Gaida
instruments.note: Goat-skin bagpipe with single drone; regional variants (džura, kaba gaida).

instruments.name: Tapan (davul)
instruments.note: Double-headed drum: mallet on one head, switch on the other.

instruments.name: Greek Bouzouki
instruments.note: Four-course (CFAD) or three-course (DAD) instrument.

instruments.name: Baglamas
instruments.note: Small bouzouki an octave higher; accompanies rebetiko.

instruments.name: Oud
instruments.note: Fretless short-neck lute; Arabic and Turkish tunings differ.

instruments.name: Bağlama (saz)
instruments.note: Long-necked fretted lute with microtonal frets; bozuk or kara düzen tuning.

instruments.name: Ney
instruments.note: End-blown reed flute; pitch shaded by embouchure and partial holing.

instruments.name: Kanun
instruments.note: Plucked trapezoid zither; mandal levers set microtonal string pitches.

instruments.name: Qanun
instruments.note: Plucked trapezoid zither; mandal (orab) levers give quarter-tone inflections.

instruments.name: Darbuka
instruments.note: Goblet drum: dum, tek and ka strokes; usul/iqa patterns.

instruments.name: Riq
instruments.note: Small frame drum with heavy jingles; ensemble timekeeper.

instruments.name: Tar (Persian)
instruments.note: Double-bowl long-neck lute with movable frets including koron intervals.

instruments.name: Setar
instruments.note: Small four-string lute played with the index fingernail; intimate tone.

instruments.name: Santur
instruments.note: Hammered dulcimer with mezrab hammers; bridges tuned to the dastgah.

instruments.name: Kamancheh
instruments.note: Spiked fiddle rotated to change strings; vocal vibrato.

instruments.name: Ney (Persian)
instruments.note: End-blown reed flute played with the teeth embouchure; distinct from Turkish ney technique.

instruments.name: Tombak (zarb)
instruments.note: Goblet drum with finger rolls and snaps.

instruments.name: Sitar
instruments.note: Movable frets, sympathetic taraf strings and chikari drones; tuned to the raga.

instruments.name: Sarod
instruments.note: Fretless metal fingerboard; glides and sympathetic strings.

instruments.name: Bansuri
instruments.note: Side-blown bamboo flute; key of the flute chosen to suit the Sa.

instruments.name: Tabla
instruments.note: Dayan tuned to Sa; bols mapped as drum strokes.

instruments.name: Tanpura / Tambura
instruments.note: Unfretted drone lute; jawari bridge; strings tuned to Pa/Ma/Ni-Sa-Sa-Sa as the raga needs.

instruments.name: Saraswati Veena
instruments.note: Fretted, with deflection-based gamaka and side drone strings.

instruments.name: Mridangam
instruments.note: Double-headed barrel drum tuned to the shruti.

instruments.name: Ghatam
instruments.note: Clay pot played with fingers, palms and the belly against the mouth.

instruments.name: Kanjira
instruments.note: Small frame drum with a single jingle pair and pitch bends.

instruments.name: Erhu
instruments.note: Two-string bowed fiddle; bow between the strings; expressive slides.

instruments.name: Pipa
instruments.note: Pear-shaped fretted lute; lun-zhi tremolo, sao and fu strums.

instruments.name: Guzheng
instruments.note: 21-string zither with movable bridges, pentatonic tuning by default.

instruments.name: Dizi
instruments.note: Transverse bamboo flute with a buzzing membrane (dimo).

instruments.name: Sheng
instruments.note: Free-reed mouth organ; plays chords and clusters.

instruments.name: Yangqin
instruments.note: Hammered dulcimer with bamboo beaters.

instruments.name: Koto
instruments.note: 13-string zither; hirajōshi or kumoijōshi tunings by moving bridges.

instruments.name: Shakuhachi
instruments.note: End-blown bamboo flute (1.8 shaku in D assumed); meri/kari pitch bending.

instruments.name: Shamisen
instruments.note: Three-string skin-headed lute played with a bachi; sawari buzz.

instruments.name: Nagadō-daiko
instruments.note: Barrel taiko; ensemble role depends on kumi-daiko or festival context.

instruments.name: Shime-daiko
instruments.note: Rope-tensioned high taiko keeping the pulse.

instruments.name: Shinobue
instruments.note: Bamboo transverse festival flute (matsuri); bright and piercing.

instruments.name: Gayageum
instruments.note: 12-string (or modern 25-string) zither; left hand presses for nonghyeon.

instruments.name: Geomungo
instruments.note: Six-string fretted zither struck with a bamboo stick (suldae).

instruments.name: Daegeum
instruments.note: Large transverse bamboo flute with a buzzing membrane (cheong).

instruments.name: Haegeum
instruments.note: Two-string vertical fiddle, no fingerboard; pressure-based pitch.

instruments.name: Piri
instruments.note: Cylindrical double-reed pipe with a wide bend range.

instruments.name: Janggu
instruments.note: Hourglass drum; jangdan rhythmic cycles.

instruments.name: Saron
instruments.note: Bronze keyed metallophone; tuned to the ensemble's own pélog or sléndro set.

instruments.name: Gendèr
instruments.note: Thin bronze keys over tube resonators; played with padded mallets and hand damping.

instruments.name: Bonang
instruments.note: Rows of horizontal kettle gongs; elaborating patterns.

instruments.name: Gong Ageng
instruments.note: Large hanging gong marking the end of the colotomic cycle; pitch set by the ensemble.

instruments.name: Kempul
instruments.note: Smaller hanging gongs subdividing the gong cycle.

instruments.name: Kenong
instruments.note: Large horizontal kettle gongs marking structural points.

instruments.name: Kendhang
instruments.note: Double-headed drum leading tempo and transitions.

instruments.name: Suling
instruments.note: Ring-duct bamboo flute; scale follows pélog or sléndro holes.

instruments.name: Gangsa
instruments.note: Bronze keyed metallophone in paired ombak (beating) tuning.

instruments.name: Reyong
instruments.note: Row of kettle gongs played by four players; interlocking figuration and accents.

instruments.name: Kendang (Balinese)
instruments.note: Paired lanang/wadon drums leading tempo changes.

instruments.name: Ceng-ceng
instruments.note: Small cymbal clusters for rhythmic texture.

instruments.name: Ranat Ek
instruments.note: Boat-shaped wooden xylophone leading the piphat.

instruments.name: Khong Wong Yai
instruments.note: Circle of kettle gongs carrying the core melody.

instruments.name: Pi Nai
instruments.note: Quadruple-reed oboe with circular breathing.

instruments.name: Taphon
instruments.note: Double-headed barrel drum played with both hands.

instruments.name: Ching
instruments.note: Small cup cymbals marking the metric cycle (open 'ching', closed 'chap').

instruments.name: Đàn tranh
instruments.note: 16-string zither; pentatonic tuning with left-hand bends.

instruments.name: Đàn bầu
instruments.note: Monochord played on harmonics; a flexible rod bends the pitch.

instruments.name: Đàn nguyệt
instruments.note: Moon-shaped two-string lute with high frets.

instruments.name: Đàn nhị
instruments.note: Two-string spike fiddle.

instruments.name: Sáo trúc
instruments.note: Transverse bamboo flute.

instruments.name: Kora
instruments.region: West Africa (Mandé: Mali, Guinea, Senegal, The Gambia)
instruments.note: 21-string bridge harp; tuning systems (e.g. silaba, tomora) are configurable.

instruments.name: Balafon
instruments.note: Wooden frame xylophone with gourd resonators and buzzing membranes; heptatonic or pentatonic tuning by maker.

instruments.name: Djembe
instruments.note: Goblet drum: bass, tone and slap strokes.

instruments.name: Dunun (dundunba, sangban, kenkeni)
instruments.note: Set of three cylinder drums with attached bells.

instruments.name: Dùndún (talking drum)
instruments.note: Hourglass tension drum whose pitch glides follow Yoruba speech tones.

instruments.name: Bàtá
instruments.note: Family of double-headed drums associated with specific orisha; some repertoire is ritually restricted.

instruments.name: Agogô / Agogo bell
instruments.note: Double iron bell carrying the timeline pattern.

instruments.name: Shekere
instruments.note: Gourd rattle with a bead net.

instruments.name: Gankogui
instruments.note: Double bell playing the timeline (bell pattern).

instruments.name: Axatse
instruments.note: Gourd rattle struck against the leg and hand.

instruments.name: Atsimevu
instruments.note: Tall master drum; lead variations signal the ensemble.

instruments.name: Sogo
instruments.note: Mid-size supporting drum, sometimes a lead.

instruments.name: Kidi
instruments.note: Smaller support drum in dialogue with the lead.

instruments.name: Kagan
instruments.note: Smallest drum, steady off-beat part.

instruments.name: Likembe
instruments.note: Box-resonated lamellophone; buzzers and tuning vary by maker and community.

instruments.name: Ngoma (Central African drum)
instruments.note: Generic placeholder for a community-specific drum; replace with the named local instrument once curated.

instruments.name: Mbira (dzavadzimu)
instruments.note: 22-28 key lamellophone in a deze resonator; nyamaropa and other tunings vary by maker.

instruments.name: Hosho
instruments.note: Paired gourd shakers in a triplet-feel pulse.

instruments.name: Marimba (Zimbabwean)
instruments.note: Diatonic marimba ensemble tradition developed from the 1960s; soprano to bass instruments.

instruments.name: Endongo
instruments.note: Bowl lyre; Baganda tuning is often described as near-equidistant pentatonic.

instruments.name: Amadinda
instruments.note: Log xylophone played by three musicians in interlocking parts.

instruments.name: Nyatiti
instruments.note: Eight-string bowl lyre; player adds a toe-ring rhythm.

instruments.name: Engoma (Baganda drums)
instruments.note: Royal and ensemble drum set; specific drums carry specific roles.

instruments.name: Bendir
instruments.note: Frame drum with a snare string under the head.

instruments.name: Guembri (gimbri / sintir)
instruments.note: Three-string bass lute with a camel-skin top; the maâlem's instrument.

instruments.name: Qraqeb (krakebs)
instruments.note: Iron double castanets in a continuous triplet pulse.

instruments.name: Ghaita (rhaita)
instruments.note: Loud conical double-reed shawm for outdoor processions.

instruments.name: Tres (Cuban)
instruments.note: Three doubled courses; carries the son montuno (guajeo).

instruments.name: Güiro
instruments.note: Scraped gourd.

instruments.name: Pandeiro
instruments.note: Tunable frame drum with jingles; full samba groove from one player.

instruments.name: Cavaquinho
instruments.note: Four-string small guitar (DGBD); rhythmic centro and solo roles.

instruments.name: Seven-String Guitar (violão de 7 cordas)
instruments.note: Nylon or steel-strung with low C (or B) string; baixaria bass counterlines.

instruments.name: Surdo
instruments.note: Deep bass drum marking beat 2 in samba.

instruments.name: Tamborim
instruments.note: Small frame drum struck with a stick.

instruments.name: Bandoneón
instruments.note: Bisonoric button concertina; bellows articulation central to tango.

instruments.name: Vihuela (Mexican)
instruments.note: Small five-string convex-backed guitar for the mariachi armonía.

instruments.name: Guitarrón
instruments.note: Six-string acoustic bass guitar; octave-doubled plucks.

instruments.name: Quena
instruments.note: Notched end-blown flute, commonly in G.

instruments.name: Siku / Zampoña
instruments.note: Panpipes split into ira and arka rows played in alternation.

instruments.name: Charango
instruments.note: Small ten-string lute with re-entrant tuning.

instruments.name: Bombo (legüero)
instruments.note: Large wooden drum played on head and rim.

instruments.name: Steel Pan (tenor / lead)
instruments.note: Lead melody pan in fourths-and-fifths layout.

instruments.name: Steel Pan (double second)
instruments.note: Pair of pans for harmony and counter-melody.

instruments.name: Steel Pan (cello / guitar pans)
instruments.note: Strumming chordal pans of the steelband.

instruments.name: Steel Pan (bass)
instruments.note: Six- to twelve-barrel bass pans.

instruments.name: Iron (engine room)
instruments.note: Brake drum struck with metal beaters; drives the engine room.
